references.text: The original regulation concerning the ransom of a half shekel for each person who was counted, which is the basis for the collection described in Exodus 38:26.
Confirms the total number of men counted in Israel: 603,550, the same figure mentioned in Exodus 38:26.
A later census in Israel that also counts men from twenty years old and upward, the same age limit as in Exodus 38:26.
Refers to the sanctuary shekel as the standard of measurement, the same standard used in Exodus 38:26.
Describes the sanctuary shekel as the standard measure for valuations, the same weight standard as in Exodus 38:26.
Jesus pays the temple tax (didrachma), which is the Greek equivalent of the half shekel required in Exodus 38:26.
Exodus 30:13 is the legislation that Exodus 38:26 shows being carried out; both confirm the tax amount (half shekel) and the principle of equality before God.
